independence: Recorded from current intended claims, source edits, provenance and native pixels before reading prior visual verdicts, detector findings or other reviewers conclusions.
coveragePolicy: Sampled paired contact sheets and any listed additional witnesses; native receipt frames exist at 30fps, but I do not claim viewing every frame.

cases.clauseCovered: Ticket over lane name (API).
cases.observation: The enlarged pale ticket visibly covers API during its rise/flight; the baseline tiny token runs below the raised API word. Only cart/API is witnessed, not every listed lane event.
cases.intendedClaim: A full-size ticket rode each lane over the lane’s name, which sat on the line on a plate; the fix set names above the lines and sent a token at 0.28 scale under them.

cases.clauseCovered: Full-size key crosses Sign-in glyphs both inbound and outbound; station-name clause unconfirmed.
cases.observation: The denser native witnesses resolve a short collision missed by the broad sheet: at frames 37–38 (+1.233–1.267 s) the large key shaft visibly crosses the S of Sign-in. Baseline half-size key clears that ink. The station name is above this path; sign-out is not captured. Supplemental valid story sign-out (64 frames/side) also shows the large shaft clipping Sign-in S at frame 24(+0.800 s), with baseline clearance.
cases.intendedClaim: The key flew to the agent, and back at sign-out, at full size over the station’s name and the lane names; the fix flies it at half size.

cases.clauseCovered: Previous exhibit remains during next request; not whole compound claim.
cases.observation: The variant retains the previous red Session-header exhibit mark through the Website ticket flight; baseline removes it before departure. The mark also drifts down and persists into the new code exhibit, a secondary effect. The closed-door subclause is not independently resolved by these samples.
cases.intendedClaim: The last event’s exhibit and closed door stayed while the next ticket travelled, and changed only when it had landed; the fix lists them in beats’ fresh, so they go before it sets off.

cases.clauseCovered: Ticket crosses station body.
cases.observation: The variant full-size ticket appears over the station circle/key and moves off across it; baseline ticket starts to the right of API and clear of the station. This witnesses expire, not all answer/request branches.
cases.intendedClaim: A request’s ticket set off from the agent’s seal and crossed the station on its way to the lane; the fix launches it on its lane, clear of the station.

cases.clauseCovered: Ticket covers API lane name on expire.
cases.observation: The expire ticket appears across API in the variant (+0.733–1.433 s); baseline starts to the right of its readable name.
cases.intendedClaim: The ticket was launched just clear of the station, so it set off over the lane’s name; the fix launches it past the name.

cases.observation: Dense frames 1,3,6,9,12,15,18 show the variant API label/line continuously climb to the upper row, while baseline retains the old API and cross-fades separately keyed new lanes. The physical slide is confirmed; whether layout motion is undesirable is editorial.
cases.intendedClaim: When the MCP lane came or went, the API lane slid to its new height: motion for the layout; the fix keys the lanes apart in the two layouts and cross-fades them.

cases.clauseCovered: Ticket flies without its lane when MCP is introduced.
cases.observation: Variant has a visible ticket crossing an empty gap from +0.733 through +2.167 s; both API and MCP strokes/names are absent. Baseline MCP stroke is visibly present throughout the flight.
cases.intendedClaim: The first fix for the sliding lanes listed them in beats’ fresh: they faded out and came back only after the ticket had travelled, so it flew on no lane; the second cross-faded them before it set off.

cases.clauseCovered: Delegation crosses station name on ascent; new-seal alternative not witnessed.
cases.observation: The variant delegation rises from below and visibly covers your agent near +0.867 s before reaching the station/seal. Baseline approaches from above, clear of the name. Only delegation remedy is witnessed.
cases.intendedClaim: A new delegation (or seal) came up from under the station, across its name, to the seal; the fix brings it from off the stage above.

The variant visibly descends nearer the station, but this cannot establish a collision with an absent exact victim. A later refresh with an already-held MCP key is outside this capture. From actual published pace origin mcpKey=true, mcp succeeds and answer is refused: nothing has been refused. Therefore no valid held-key refresh film exists in the requested history.

supplement.reason: From actual published pace origin mcpKey=true, mcp succeeds and answer is refused: nothing has been refused. Therefore no valid held-key refresh film exists in the requested history.

cases.clauseCovered: Changed diagonal entry and clock-label occlusion confirmed; exact stamp-body crossing unconfirmed.

cases.clauseCovered: Published key fails to travel to wax before the ticket checks it causes.
cases.observation: Baseline visibly moves ring down before the ticket arrives. Variant keeps the ring in the chain throughout ticket travel, arrival and punched checks, then relocates it to wax only near settle (+3.4–3.9 s).
cases.intendedClaim: When the published key pressed the seal, nothing showed it moving: it left the chain and appeared on the wax only as the picture settled, after the punches it caused; the fix sends it down first.

cases.clauseCovered: Published ring shown in chain and travelling/on wax at once.
cases.observation: At +0.967 s the variant shows both a hanging published ring and its white travelling ring; at +1.467 s onward the old ring and ring over wax remain simultaneously visible. Baseline leaves an empty ring slot during transfer.
cases.intendedClaim: The published key flew to the wax while it still hung in the chain, so it was in two places; the fix takes it out of the chain as the trip begins.

cases.clauseCovered: Squeezing cannot be visually reproduced because runtime refuses the transition.
cases.observation: Baseline send films normally. Variant receipt records RangeError before the first transition paint: authored 3.060 s exceeds 2.600 s event. Only the preceding resting frame exists. This is an early refusal, not filmed compressed fades.
cases.intendedClaim: Every tamper ran in a fixed 2.6 s runTime, while its beats lasted 3.1 s (4.35 s with the published key’s trip), so they were squeezed into it; the fix gives each transition its own length. Undone with the beats as they were then.

cases.clauseCovered: Longer4.35 s published-key sequence confirmed; subjective too-long judgment remains editorial.
cases.observation: The published-key transition now actually films: native ledger gives baseline 3.9 s and variant 4.35 s; variant remains unfinished at baseline completion and settles later. No squeezed fade or collision is established. Whether this additional 0.45 s is too long is an editorial pacing judgment; the historical3.1 s ordinary tamper branch is not this capture.
cases.intendedClaim: A tamper took 3.1 s, and 4.35 s with the published key’s trip; the last audit commit shortened every beat.

cases.clauseCovered: People move for page-opening layout; undesired-motion interpretation editorial.
cases.observation: Variant keeps the agent/key/tag near the top while the new page appears, then moves them down through the page near +3.067–4.1 s. Baseline first cross-fades those people to the lower layout and the page opens clear. The moving variant tag/station visibly crosses page text, a concrete secondary obstruction.
cases.intendedClaim: When the page opened, you and the agent slid to your places beside it, motion that says nothing about the protocol; the fix cross-fades them.

cases.clauseCovered: People slide back on collect; not an objective protocol-state error.
cases.observation: After the page closes, variant people remain below while the returned key/tag settle above, then people travel upward near the end. Baseline fades people out below and reintroduces them in the upper layout. The physical layout slide is visible; the judgment that it adds no protocol meaning is editorial.
cases.intendedClaim: When the page closed after the code came back, you and the agent slid back across the stage; the fix cross-fades them.

cases.clauseCovered: 4.8 s token-return duration; current baseline 4.45 s, not3.3 s.

cases.clauseCovered: Full-size direct request and object obstruction confirmed; exact agent-side label obstruction not established.

Incidental object contact does not confirm the historical labels clause.

cases.clauseCovered: No password readable before the card on current reask approval.
cases.observation: Both sides start with a fresh unapproved page (before.sign.approved=null after a new ask); both fields are empty during the moving card and receive password dots only as it arrives. No already-approved field survives this route. A repeated approval within one sign-in is not witnessed here. From actual published sign-out origin, ask and approve-read are accepted but approve-all is refused: you have answered this sign-in already. The hypothesized same-sign second approval is not reachable by this log.
cases.intendedClaim: The password in the page was not listed in beats’ fresh, so on a second approval it stayed in the field while your card was still on its way to it; the fix lists it.

supplement.reason: From actual published sign-out origin, ask and approve-read are accepted but approve-all is refused: you have answered this sign-in already. The hypothesized same-sign second approval is not reachable by this log.

cases.clauseCovered: Shorter fades/event duration; historical beats-overrun/squeezing unconfirmed.

baselineConclusion: No baseline regression observed in these sampled targeted witnesses. This is not an exhaustive all-setting/all-history or continuous-playback certification.
captureLimits: 800×450 native scene at 30 fps; paired same-offset contact samples, with dense manually selected native crops where listed. Complete transition frame ledgers exist for all completed sides; sessions-squeezed variant has only the preceding resting frame. Caption holds/history outside selected transitions are not visually exhausted. No live phone/browser assessment was performed.
